answer.rationale: Rollback is excluded by compliance mandate on the security patch, removing the option memory_b1 would otherwise support. Regional failover (memory_b2) is tempting since degradation is confined to the primary region, but shifting a payments write path during peak settlement risks dropped or duplicated writes if failover isn't fully write-consistent — that conflicts with the objective of not losing customer writes. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) fits partner-dependency failures, not an internally climbing write-path p99, so it's not clearly applicable here. Read replica routing (memory_b5) only offloads read traffic and won't relieve write-path latency. Adding capacity to the primary region directly targets a resource-bound write-path bottleneck without moving live transactional traffic, which best protects write durability during peak settlement. I want to verify memory_b3's original context to confirm it addressed write-path (not just read/query) headroom under peak load, and verify memory_b2 to check whether that failover preserved write integrity or was read/latency-only, since misapplying either analogy under compliance and peak-write constraints is the main risk. Given the stakes (settlement/payments) and only one intervention slot, I favor a small guarded capacity addition first rather than a broad rollout or a riskier regional shift.
